cells.tense: Right now, with the whole thing in view.
cells.verb: seeing all of it, nothing left out
cells.place: in what you're carrying and how long you've carried it
cells.ask: Let what you see show — tell one person the whole shape of what you're holding, not to be helped, just so the seeing is out in the room.
cells.core:
You can see the whole of what you're carrying — the weight, the length of it, what it costs — and you're still carrying it. Knowing didn't break the hold and holding didn't dim the knowing. That's the rare part: most people get one or the other.

What this is free to do next isn't more carrying. It's letting the seeing be visible. Say the whole shape of it to someone, plainly, once — not to hand any of it over, just so what you understand isn't locked inside the endurance. You don't have to make a point of it. It shows on its own when you stop keeping it in.
cells.sheetLine: You see all of what you're holding, and you're still holding it.

cells.tense: You're living in how it ends.
cells.verb: reading the whole thing to its last page
cells.place: in a weight that hasn't finished arriving
cells.ask: Pick up the next piece of this as if you haven't read the ending — let one moment be the first one, with nothing decided about it yet.
cells.core:
You've already seen how this carrying goes — every turn, every cost, the way it finishes — and you're bracing against all of it at once. The seeing ran ahead of the weight. So you're holding tomorrow's load with today's back, and the holding has gone hard because there's nothing left to find out.

The way back isn't to see less. It's to meet one thing before you've finished it. Take the next piece as if it's new, as if you don't know how it lands, and let it be that for a minute. Clear sight that can still be surprised doesn't have to brace. It just sees, and keeps carrying, and doesn't need the ending in hand to prove it can.
cells.sheetLine: You've already read the ending, and you're carrying it early.

cells.tense: You stopped looking a while back.
cells.verb: holding without looking at what's held
cells.place: in a weight you're still bearing
cells.ask: Choose one small thing to make out of what you're carrying — the first concrete step of it — and start that, without needing to see the rest.
cells.core:
You're still carrying it. You just don't look at it anymore. Somewhere behind you, seeing the whole of the weight felt like more than you could hold, so you set the seeing down and kept the load. The hold is steady; it's also blind now. You can't tell what's still yours, what's grown, what's finished.

Looking straight at it won't work from here — that door is behind you. What pulls the seeing back is a decision, small and solid: pick one thing you'll do with what you carry, the first real piece of it, and begin. Direction lights up what it's pointed at. Once you're choosing again, you'll find you can see the whole of it and not go dim.
cells.sheetLine: You're still holding it. You've stopped seeing what it is.

cells.tense: You know, and you're saying you don't.
cells.verb: seeing the whole shape of it
cells.place: in what you've been carrying as just getting through
cells.ask: Say the plainest true thing you can see about what you carry — one sentence, the simplest one — out loud, and let it be yours.
cells.core:
You already see it. The full shape of what you're carrying, what it's cost, how long — it's all there, and it's steering how you hold. But you'd call this just getting through, one day at a time, nothing to look at. The understanding is complete. You're treating it as if it never happened.

The way back is smaller than the whole picture. Go to the first thing you noticed — the simplest, most obvious fact about this weight — and say it, once, as something you see. Not the full account. Just the first cut. When the seeing is owned, it doesn't need to be argued or hidden; it shows in how you carry, and you get to be the one who knows.
cells.sheetLine: You already see all of it. You're calling it getting by.
